intro: Here is Nysa, an ancient city in Aydın province whose story runs from the 3rd century BC to the 6th century AD. It lies near Sultanhisar, and it is known for its tunnel-lined street and its grand library.
history: Founded in the Hellenistic period, Nysa became a wealthy cultural centre of the Maeander valley. Its huge library and the tunnel-lined basilica street still show the splendour the city reached in the Roman era.
structure-2: You are now at the Tunnel Street. A vaulted stone tunnel was built over the stream that divides the city, and on top of it ran the city's street and square. Think of it: daily life went on above, while the water flowed beneath.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Library and the Theatre, and make your way to the Stadium and the Gymnasium too.
facts: Did you know? The library at Nysa is the second-largest ancient library in Anatolia after the Library of Celsus at Ephesus. The vaulted tunnel carrying the city over its ravine runs about 100 metres, among the longest bridge vaults of antiquity. The geographer Strabo studied here as a young man and described the city from first-hand observation. And the council house survives almost intact, marble seating and all.
outro: This brings our tour of Nysa to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Enjoy your visit.
